Label each block with its majority-group cluster

Source: R/seg_clusters.R
seg_cluster_blocks.Rd

Runs the same cluster search as seg_clusters() and returns the blocks with each one's cluster, for mapping or for checking a place by hand.

Usage

seg_cluster_blocks(
  blocks,
  by,
  group,
  total,
  threshold = 0.5,
  bridge_empty = TRUE,
  contiguity = c("rook", "queen")
)

Arguments

blocks

An sf object with one row per block, such as the output of seg_blocks().

by

<tidy-select> Column or columns identifying the unit, such as place_geoid. Blocks with a missing value in any by column are dropped.

group, total

<data-masking> Block counts of the group and of the whole population. group must not exceed total.

threshold

A block qualifies when the group's share of its population is strictly above threshold. The default, 0.5, means a majority.

bridge_empty

Should blocks with no population join clusters? The default, TRUE, lets them; FALSE is a robustness setting. See Details.

contiguity

"rook" (the default) treats blocks as adjacent when they share an edge; "queen" also counts a shared corner.

Value

blocks without the rows that have a missing by value, plus an integer column cluster: 1 for the unit's most populous cluster, 2 for the next, and so on, and NA for blocks in no cluster. Empty blocks that bridge clusters carry the label of the cluster they join.

See also

seg_clusters() for one summary row per unit.

Examples

blocks <- sf::st_sf(
  place = "a",
  latino = c(60, 70, 0, 80, 10),
  total = c(100, 100, 0, 100, 100),
  geometry = sf::st_make_grid(cellsize = 1, offset = c(0, 0), n = c(5, 1))
)
seg_cluster_blocks(blocks, by = place, group = latino, total = total)
#> Simple feature collection with 5 features and 4 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 5 ymax: 1
#> CRS:           NA
#>   place latino total                       geometry cluster
#> 1     a     60   100 POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 ...       1
#> 2     a     70   100 POLYGON ((1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 1 ...       1
#> 3     a      0     0 POLYGON ((2 0, 3 0, 3 1, 2 ...       1
#> 4     a     80   100 POLYGON ((3 0, 4 0, 4 1, 3 ...       1
#> 5     a     10   100 POLYGON ((4 0, 5 0, 5 1, 4 ...      NA
